title: Is there a largest common multiple of two numbers?
description: The common toran lengths of six and eight are listed again and found to go on without end, so there is no largest one. Only the lowest common multiple, twenty four, can be named. Keeko doubts this and wants ninety six as the largest, where the list happens to stop.
teaching_notes: One idea: adding twenty four to any common multiple of six and eight gives a bigger common multiple, so the list never ends. Watch for students who think a list is complete because they stopped writing it.

source: Is there a largest common multiple of 6 and 8? Explain, and name the lowest.
video_script.why: The child has found the shortest toran both makers can make and now asks whether a longest one exists.
video_script.substitution: Add the lowest common multiple to any common multiple to get a bigger one, so the list never ends.
video_script.anchor: The common toran lengths of 6 cm and 8 cm strips written in a row: 24, 48, 72, 96 and so on, with an arrow pointing on past the last one.
video_script.wrong_answer: the largest common multiple is ninety six
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes ninety six as the largest common multiple because the written list stops there, but adding twenty four gives one hundred twenty, which is larger.
video_script.payoff_line: There is no largest common multiple, and the lowest is twenty four

final_answer.value: No largest; the LCM of 6 and 8 is 24
final_answer.spoken: there is no largest common multiple, and the lowest is twenty four

names.Ruhee: makes torans with 6 cm strips of cloth
names.Jia: makes torans with 8 cm strips of cloth

never_show: 96 as the largest common multiple, marked right
maths_rules: common multiples of 6 and 8: 24, 48, 72, 96 and so on
24 = 4 × 6 and 24 = 3 × 8, so adding 24 to a multiple of 6 gives a multiple of 6, and the same for 8
so 24 added to any common multiple gives a bigger common multiple, and the list never ends
the lowest common multiple of 6 and 8 is 24
slip: 96 + 24 = 120, which is a common multiple larger than 96
video_script.design: One idea: adding the lowest common multiple always gives another common multiple, so there is no largest. The list stays on the board with an arrow that continues past the last number.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Ruhee and Jia make torans with strips of six and eight centimetres.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A length that both can make is called a common multiple. Twenty four and forty eight are two of them.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Is there a largest common multiple? And which one is the lowest?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A list of multiples can always be written one place further.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The first common multiple in the list, the smallest one, is called the lowest common multiple.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We ask whether the list of common multiples ever stops.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, write the common multiples of six and eight.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks the largest common multiple is ninety six, because the list stops there.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But ninety six plus twenty four is one hundred twenty, and that is a common multiple too.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The list stops only because we stopped writing. The lowest one is the only one we can name.
